Triage (2026-09-20T15:44Z): lands in `domain:cli` · `priority:p2` · type `Bug`.

**Lane `domain:cli`.** `packages/cli/test/union-fold-command-parity.test.ts` and the two passes that decayed it (`runPerPackageAuthoringRules` on `validate` and `lint`) are all `packages/cli`, which the 域车道 table assigns to this lane.

**Grade `p2`, and it is for the MEASURED instance, ⛔ not for the generalisation.** 北极星's 仪器 test is answerable here with one of its four named answers — 「一次放过假货的复核」: the control was a true pin of `authoringRuleUnionStack` at #17069 and stopped being one when #18677 and #18778 put a sibling pass on the same doors, so its assertion is now satisfiable by a mechanism that is ⛔ not the one under test. A pin that passes for the wrong reason is worse than a missing pin, because the roster still counts it. ⇒ 能跑但出错 ⇒ `p2`.

Type `Bug`: the control declares what it pins and pins something else.

## ⭐ The property that makes this worth a card rather than a test fix

「**No commit to that file ever weakened it.** The control did not change, its fixture did not change, and no review of either could have caught it.」 ⇒ the decay arrived from OUTSIDE the file, through a sibling mechanism reaching the same doors later. That is a class no diff review can see, which is exactly why the generalisation is interesting — and exactly why it is ⛔ not this card's deliverable.

## ⚠️ Two halves, and only one of them is graded here

1. **The measured instance** — repair `union-fold-command-parity` so ablating the union fold alone turns it red. That is what `p2` is on and what a claimant delivers.
2. **The repo-wide sweep** — 「ablate both to turn red」 as a general property of controls. The delivering dev declined to file this itself and was right to: 「a repo-wide sweep is a scope proposal rather than a reproducible defect」. ⇒ if the lane wants it, it goes to the decision box as a scope card with its own measurement of how many controls could be affected. ⛔ It is not licence for the claimant of (1) to widen.

⚠️ The repair has a named shape on the card — pin by the finding's **pedigree prefix** (union vs per-package) rather than by rule/path/code, so the two mechanisms stop being interchangeable at the assertion. Take that reading again at claim time; the two passes may have moved since #19369.

Size/model suggestion: S.

## ⭐ The deliverable is a VERDICT, ⛔ not a gate

This card records a class:

> a control can be **correct when written** and decay into an impostor-satisfied one with **no edit to it or its fixture**, because a sibling mechanism reaches the same doors later.

⛔ **Do not open this as a repo-wide test audit.** The #18897 sweep already ablated **21** `packages/cli` fixtures across **30 legs** and **9 mechanisms** and found exactly **one** instance. The base rate does not pay for a blanket sweep, and the card says so.

⭐ What is valuable is the **trigger**, not the sweep:

> when a PR **adds a mechanism to a door**, ask which existing controls assert something about that door's output.

**Whether that is mechanisable is the question this round answers.** ⭐ *"No, and here is precisely why"* is a **complete and valuable outcome** — the same shape as #19246, which discharged by measuring that its card did not reproduce.

## What you have to work from

The one worked instance, with full data in #18897's landing record (`5750712407`) and PR #19369:

- `union-fold-command-parity.test.ts` was a **true** pin of `authoringRuleUnionStack` at #17069;
- it stopped being one when **#18677** and **#18778** put `runPerPackageAuthoringRules` on `validate` and `lint` — the same rule, same path, same refusal code on that fixture;
- ablation: fold alone → 6/6 green; per-package alone → 6/6 green; **both** → 3 red;
- ⛔ **no commit to that file ever weakened it**, and both #18677 and #18778 were correct work.

## The questions to answer, in order

1. **Is "a PR adds a mechanism to a door" detectable at all?** What would the signal be — a new call site into an existing dispatch/registration path? ⛔ Do not assume it is a diff-shape question; measure what the one known instance actually looked like as a diff.
2. **Given a detected door change, can "which controls assert something about that door's output" be derived** — or does it require knowing what each control *means*? ⚠️ If the honest answer is the latter, say so; that is the verdict.
3. **What would a false positive cost?** ⭐ A trigger that fires on every PR touching a shared path is worse than no trigger, because it trains people to dismiss it.

## ⛔ Fences

⛔ Do not build and land a gate in this round. If your verdict is "mechanisable", the deliverable is the **design plus the evidence**, and the seat dispatches the build separately.
⛔ Do not modify any existing test or fixture. ⛔ Never edit `content/docs/releases/`.
⚠️ If you write a probe to measure feasibility, it is a **throwaway** — say so, and prove the tree is clean afterwards.
Changeset: likely none, since a measurement round may change no shipped byte — ⛔ but derive it from the repo's gates rather than assuming, and ⛔ do not name a level here before you know whether anything ships.
Commit trailers **model-free**: `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` plus a `Claude-Session:` line. English. If there is a diff, draft PR with `Fixes #19371`; if there is none, report and the seat closes the card on your measurement.

⚠️ If any part of this order is imprecise or contradicts what you measure, **say so and stop rather than silently matching it** — five of this seat's orders were wrong this shift and a dev caught every one.

## The verdict

**Not mechanisable as the card phrases it.** The honest answer is the one the card names as a complete outcome: half the derivation requires knowing what each control *means*. Everything below is measured over `objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `origin/main` `43d492ff98c1`, window **2026-08-21 to 2026-09-20**, proven covered by `scripts/pm/git-history.mjs ensure` (floor 2026-08-14) -- **3785** first-parent commits.

### First, a translation the questions need

`#18677` and `#18778` are **cards**. The diffs are **PR #18769** (`095c7f60ae`) and **PR #18813** (`9bd631f3ff`). #18769 did two things in one commit: it *extracted* `runPerPackageAuthoringRules` out of `compile.ts` into `utils/artifact-packages.ts`, and it added the second call site on `validate`. So the causing diff reads as an ordinary refactor-plus-fix.

### Q1 -- detectable, but only at symbol granularity, and only where a door is a directory

| signal | fires / 30 days | catches both instances |
|---|---|---|
| touches `packages/cli/src/commands/` at all | **207** | yes |
| adds any import line to a non-test command module | **56** | yes |
| **module-edge**: new import of a specifier a sibling command module already imports (relative only) | **19** | **NO -- misses #18813** |
| **symbol-level**: new named binding a sibling command module already imports | **18** | yes |
| the above, minus fires whose target command file is new in the same commit | **14** | yes |
| the above, restricted to bindings 2 or more sibling doors already import | **8** | yes |

The third row is the load-bearing negative. "A new call site into an existing dispatch path", read the natural way as a **module import edge**, has a **50% false-negative rate on the one known instance**: at `9bd631f3ff^`, `lint.ts` line 18 already read `import { artifactPackages, packageBodyAsStack } from '../utils/artifact-packages.js'` -- for its own intra-package duplicate-name advisory, per that PR's own body. #18813 added a *binding*, not an *edge*. So any implementation must parse import clauses or call sites, never module specifiers.

The 8-fire signal is real, not noise-driven: the window contains **three** instances of the same family -- `authoringRuleUnionStack` reaching `validate` and `lint` (#17524, `edaf3b2f78`), `lowerCallables` reaching `validate` then `lint` (`6b7d709b87`, `0cde37d788`), and the pair under study. The signal finds a genuine recurring shape. It is the **follow-up** that does not pay.

⚠️ Thresholds were chosen after seeing the answer. 8 per 30 days is therefore a **floor** on the out-of-sample rate, not an estimate of it. And `packages/cli/src/commands/` is one door family that happens to be an enumerable directory; it is 207 of the 2038 window commits touching any `packages/*/src`. REST routes, kernel registration and driver dispatch have no such directory, so a repo-wide trigger needs a hand-maintained door register -- the meaning problem, relocated.

### Q2 -- the derivation splits, and only the cheap half is mechanical

**Half A, "which controls assert something about that door's output": derivable.** At `095c7f60ae^`, **24** of 328 `packages/cli` test files attach to the validate/lint doors -- 22 spawn the binary with `validate` or `lint` in argv, 2 import the command module. The victim is in the set.

**Half B, "which of those the new mechanism can now satisfy": not derivable.** Two independent measurements:

**(i) The claimed-mechanism mapping does not exist mechanically.** Extracting backticked identifiers from a control's leading docblock and resolving them against the 1242 exported symbols of `packages/cli/src` plus `packages/lint/src`:

| population | names exactly one | names none | names several |
|---|---|---|---|
| all 340 `packages/cli` test files | 71 (21%) | **222 (65%)** | 47 (14%) |
| the 24 controls on this door | 10 | **11** | 3 |

Of the 10 that name exactly one, most name a printer, a type or a constant -- `emitJson`, `LintIssue`, `TEMPLATES`, `errorCodeFields` -- not a mechanism. The victim is the lucky case: its pre-repair docblock named exactly one exported symbol, `authoringRuleUnionStack`. Its own named sibling, `authoring-rule-command-parity.test.ts`, names **none**.

**(ii) The ablation is semantic, and the two mechanisms on this very door prove it.** `authoringRuleUnionStack` has a generic identity-shaped signature -- stack in, stack out -- and its neutral form is *return the input unchanged*. `runPerPackageAuthoringRules` returns a findings record and its neutral form is *return nothing*. A generic mutation engine cannot choose between them, and choosing wrong makes the leg meaningless in both directions: identity-ablating the per-package pass does not typecheck, empty-ablating the fold destroys every door at once. One hand-authored neutral form **per mechanism** is unavoidable.

⇒ **the honest answer to Q2 is the latter, and that is the verdict.**

### Q3 -- what a false positive costs, quantified

**8** fires per 30 days on `packages/cli/src/commands` alone, each asking for Half B over **24** controls: **192 non-mechanical judgements per 30 days**, one package, one door family, roughly one interruption every 3.75 days.

Against that: **one** known instance in the window, surfaced by the #18897 sweep, not by any trigger. Per-fire precision is therefore **at most 12.5%**, and that bound is generous because it credits the fire for a find the trigger did not make. The other 6 fires' follow-ups -- 144 judgements -- are **NOT MEASURED**, not clean: nobody ran them.

For scale, the #18897 sweep judged 21 controls by property across 30 ablation legs and 9 mechanisms to find that one instance. The trigger would demand roughly **9 times that judgement volume per month**, on one package's doors, with no ablation legs behind it -- pure reading. That is exactly the rate at which the card says a trigger becomes worse than none.

### The reframe -- the part worth keeping

The card binds detection to the **causing PR**. But the causing PR is correct work whose diff contains nothing about the victim, and asking a reviewer to reason about 24 other files is the expensive half. **Detection does not need the causing PR at all.**

The decay is directly observable as a **red-to-green flip in an ablation matrix**: for each mechanism M, record which control cases die when M alone is ablated; a cell that was red and is now green, on a control nobody edited, is the alarm.

- It is **meaning-free at detection time** -- no claimed-mechanism mapping is needed, which is what kills the per-PR trigger.
- It is **O(mechanisms), not O(mechanisms squared)**. Read off this card's own table: ablating the union fold **alone** already left the control 6/6 green. The pair was needed to explain the cause, never to detect it.
- Its false positive is a **named cell**, not "audit 24 controls", and the legitimate flips (control edited, fixture edited, mechanism renamed) are filterable by the diff.
- Its cost is one recomputation of roughly the #18897 sweep's size -- a **periodic job, not a per-PR gate**. ⛔ **NOT MEASURED**: wall-clock of one recomputation. Pricing it would have cost a shared-container build lap for a round that produces no diff.
- Its preconditions are the honest catch: one hand-authored neutral form per mechanism, and a mechanism register -- the same register a repo-wide trigger would have needed.

⛔ **Not built.** The fences forbid it and the seat dispatches it separately if it wants it.

### The cheap thing that already works

PR #19369's repair is the zero-per-PR-cost form of the same idea: `runPerPackageAuthoringRules` **owns** the `package 'PACKAGE_ID' -- ` prefix on every finding it raises, so a control can assert the absence of a pedigree it must not carry. Generalised: **a mechanism that can reach a door someone else's control asserts on should own a marker in its output.**

⚠️ It is not universal, and the victim's own docblock says why: a real falsifier -- a fixture the impostor structurally cannot reach -- does not exist for this rule class, because the per-package pass is a superset of the union run for reference rules. The pedigree is load-bearing there only because it is **paired with a positive control**. An unpaired negative assertion would be satisfied by a prefix the suite never produces at all.

### Round state

No diff, so no PR, no changeset and no labels. **Changeset class: there is no diff to classify.** `skip-changeset` is a label for a *diff* that publishes nothing; with an empty diff the question does not arise, and `dispatch-gates.mjs` derives no gate family. Had the verdict landed as a `docs/audits/` record instead, the class would be `skip-changeset` -- no package manifest's `files` array reaches `docs/`, and the root package is private -- but writing that file was not asked for and would be scope this card fences off.

The branch `claude/issue-19371-control-decay-trigger-feasibility` is pushed and empty (identical to `origin/main`); it is the claim comment's landing marker and carries no PR. Delete it at will.

## Seat closeout — **VERDICT: not mechanisable at useful precision.** The card is discharged by a measurement, ⛔ not by a build.

⭐ This is the outcome the dispatch named as complete: *"'No, and here is precisely why' is a complete and valuable outcome."* ⛔ No gate was built, no test was touched, and there is no diff — `git status --porcelain` empty, `dispatch-gates --commands` exits 2 with *"this branch changes nothing against origin/main — nothing to derive."*

### Q1 — the door change is detectable, but only at symbol granularity

⚠️ **The natural signal is the one that fails.** A module-import-edge check **misses PR #18813 outright**, because `lint.ts` **already imported the helper module** at line 18 for its own duplicate-name advisory. The edge existed before the mechanism arrived.

The tightest purely mechanical signal fires **8 times per 30 days** on `packages/cli/src/commands` alone — ⚠️ and its thresholds are **hindsight-tuned to this instance**, so **8 is a floor**, not an estimate.

### Q2 — half the derivation is semantic, which is the verdict

*"Which controls assert about that door's output"* **is** derivable: **24** controls were attached to the validate/lint doors at the moment of decay.

*"Which of those the new mechanism can now satisfy"* is **not**:

- only **10 of 24** name exactly one exported symbol in their leading docblock, and most of those name a **printer, a type or a constant**;
- ⭐ **the ablation itself is semantic** — the two mechanisms on this very door need **opposite** neutral forms: `authoringRuleUnionStack` ablates to **identity**, `runPerPackageAuthoringRules` ablates to **empty**. ⇒ no mechanical rule produces both.

### Q3 — the precision bound, and why it is generous

**8 fires × 24 controls = 192 non-mechanical judgements per 30 days**, on **one package's one door family**, against **1** known instance.

⇒ per-fire precision **at most 12.5%** — ⚠️ and that bound is **generous**, because it credits the fire for a find the **#18897 sweep** actually made, not the trigger.

⭐ This is the answer to Q3 as asked: a trigger firing 8×/month at ≤12.5% precision **trains people to dismiss it**, which is worse than no trigger.

## ⭐ The reframe — the round's real residue

> **Detection does not need the causing PR at all.**

The decay is directly observable as a **red-to-green flip in an ablation matrix**, which is:

- **meaning-free at detection time** — the semantic work moves to *explaining* a flip, ⛔ not to finding one;
- **O(mechanisms), ⛔ not O(mechanisms²)** — single ablation of the union fold alone already left the control **6/6 green**, read straight off this card's own table. ⇒ ⭐ **the pair was needed to explain the cause and never to detect it.**

⇒ that is a **periodic job**, ⛔ not a per-PR gate. Preconditions: one hand-authored neutral form per mechanism, plus a mechanism register.

⛔ **Not built** — the dispatch fenced it out, and the decision to build is a separate one. Recorded as **#19409**, with the base-rate argument *against* it stated alongside.

## ⚠️ A correction to this seat's order, recorded rather than buried

The card body and my dispatch both read as though **#18677 and #18778** were the PRs that put `runPerPackageAuthoringRules` on the doors. **They are the CARDS.** The diffs are **PR #18769** (`095c7f60ae`, `os validate`) and **PR #18813** (`9bd631f3ff`, `os lint`) — verified by this seat: both merged with matching titles, and both issues return `is_pr: false`.

⇒ my order said *"measure what #18677 and #18778 actually looked like as diffs"*, and **an issue has no diff** — the instruction was literally unsatisfiable. ⭐ The dev performed the translation and **recorded it as a required first step** rather than silently doing it. That is the sixth order imprecision this shift and the sixth a dev has flagged.

⚠️ Citing cards is this repo's norm, so the card body is not wrong; ⛔ but an order that asks for a **diff** must name the **PR**.

`pm:dispatched` stripped and the assignee cleared in one write, read back. The card is discharged: the question it asked has a measured answer.
